synthesis: Completion and centering turn the scalar reflection s -> 1-s into evenness about the critical-line coordinate while separating the pole and trivial factors from the nontrivial-zero question; this organizes the zero set but supplies no reality mechanism.
source_support: Bombieri states the meromorphic zeta package, completed entire even xi function, trivial/nontrivial distinction, and equivalence of RH with reality of xi zeros. Riemann's assigned units derive the completed reflection by contour reversal and then define the centered xi through an even cosine kernel.
nonparaphrase_operation: Track the representation change from zeta(s), through completion, to the centered t-coordinate: reflection becomes sign reversal and then visible evenness, while the conjectural location statement remains strictly stronger than the symmetry.
limits: The functional-equation and integral displays are extraction-sensitive, and none of the parents excludes symmetric off-line zero pairs or proves RH.
quality_reason: All parents support distinct stages of the same completion-and-centering mechanism, and the synthesis explicitly blocks the false implication from reflection symmetry or evenness to critical-line localization.

synthesis: Idempotent splitting makes the bicomplex construction componentwise, but its hyperbolic restriction feeds zeta only real scalar arguments and therefore retains only the real trivial zeros; algebraic transparency can thus erase the nonreal zero geometry that the classical xi representation preserves as the RH problem.
source_support: The Clay unit identifies nontrivial zeta zeros and the equivalent xi reality problem. The bicomplex units give unique idempotent channels with componentwise holomorphic reconstruction and show that the hyperbolic restriction has exactly the trivial zero lattice because both projected arguments are real.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compare what two representation changes preserve: xi centers and retains the nontrivial-zero problem, whereas hyperbolic projection restricts both scalar channels to the real line and deletes access to nonreal zeros.
limits: This applies to the source's specific hyperbolic restriction, not every bicomplex or hyperbolic zeta construction; it neither contradicts the classical theory nor proves RH or classifies a full bicomplex critical-line analogue.
quality_reason: The relation is a concrete preserve-versus-forget audit grounded in the projected arguments, not a generic analogy between extensions, and it carries the incompatible-domain boundary explicitly.

synthesis: Prime-power-weighted coordinates trade direct prime identity for compatibility with factorial products, logarithmic differentiation, and explicit transforms; in Riemann's reciprocal-weighted coordinate the aggregation is also exactly reversible by a squarefree alternating transform.
source_support: Bombieri's span reports weighted counts tied to an exact factorial identity and correct-order bounds; Moree defines theta, psi, and Lambda and connects logarithmic differentiation to the prime-zero explicit formula; Riemann states the squarefree signed inversion from f back to F.
nonparaphrase_operation: Separate three operations rather than equating their weights: product-compatible logarithmic weighting, analytic linearization through -zeta'/zeta and test functions, and Mobius-type cancellation that reverses Riemann's particular prime-power smoothing.
limits: The weights, transforms, hypotheses, and recovery claims are not interchangeable; only Riemann's stated f-to-F relation supplies exact inversion here, and analytic convenience neither locates zeros nor identifies a prime from a positive weighted increment.
quality_reason: The synthesis extracts a reusable aggregation-and-recovery pattern while preserving the sources' different coordinates and avoiding the overclaim that every weighted prime-power statistic is invertible.

synthesis: A finite RH certificate requires both localization of critical-line zeros and an independently justified total zero count; indexed range stitching, a terminal overrun, and conservative value enclosures are computational layers that can feed that dual certificate.
source_support: Bombieri and Moree distinguish detected critical zeros from the argument-principle count of all zeros. The 1986 computation records an inherited prefix, adjacent new Gram-index ranges, five extra Rosser-valid blocks, and an imported theorem yielding the finite result; its error unit gives conservative bounds and reports sign determination at every required Gram point.
nonparaphrase_operation: Decompose certification into a local sign record, composable coverage coordinates, endpoint evidence, and a global count/conversion theorem, then require equality rather than treating sampled roots as complete.
limits: The exact role of the five-block overrun remains inside the cited theorem, numerical signs alone do not certify completeness, and the result is confined to the verified rectangle with boundary and nonvanishing assumptions.
quality_reason: Every cited parent supports a necessary layer of the finite certificate, and the synthesis retains the imported theorem and total-count obligations instead of promoting a large sign computation to global RH evidence.

synthesis: A Hilbert-Polya realization needs more than a relabeling of zeros: it needs a natural carrier, an operator correspondence, and an independent sign, positivity, or selfadjointness mechanism. Connes's cokernel and the finite-difference Hamiltonian instantiate different correspondence mechanisms while leaving spectral reality as a separate burden.
source_support: Bombieri frames cohomology, Frobenius, and index roles as missing speculative structures. Connes demands a noncircular natural pair and proves, in the assigned cokernel, that L-function zeros support annihilating distributions and generalized eigenvectors. The Hamiltonian units state a formal boundary-selected zero correspondence and conditional exceptional-point behavior while explicitly leaving domain and selfadjointness open.
nonparaphrase_operation: Factor the spectral program into naturality, zero-to-spectrum transport, multiplicity/Jordan encoding, and a reality-enforcing theorem; compare which factors each proposal supplies and which it does not.
limits: Connes's spectral identification is not a positivity theorem, the Hamiltonian claims are formal and conditional on unresolved domain and correspondence issues, and neither construction in these units proves RH.
quality_reason: The comparison preserves the proposals' incompatible constructions and epistemic statuses while extracting a concrete requirements audit, rather than treating all spectral language as an equivalent solution.

synthesis: Riemann's factorwise inversion reduces heterogeneous completed-zeta contributions to one parameterized kernel, the quantum-chaos source assigns prime powers formal orbit-action labels, and Connes supplies a general graph-diagonal mechanism by which transverse return maps produce trace weights. Together they define a trace-formula program, not an identification of primes with constructed classical orbits.
source_support: Riemann explicitly states the common beta-parameter form for nonconstant factor contributions. The quantum-chaos unit gives the Gutzwiller-like prime-power/action correspondence and says the Hamiltonian is unknown. Connes derives periodic-orbit and isolated-flow-zero contributions from graph/diagonal transversality and transverse determinants.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compare two source-specific normalizations of many local terms into one reusable analytic or geometric rule, with the formal prime-power labels occupying the still-missing arithmetic-to-dynamics interface.
limits: Connes's assigned derivation is a general flow trace mechanism and does not construct arithmetic orbits; Riemann's damaged kernel is not equated with the return-map determinant, and no Hamiltonian, orbit identification, or RH proof follows.
quality_reason: Accepted only as a bounded mechanism-level program: the synthesis explicitly denies the false equivalence between the inverse-transform kernel, a generic flow determinant, and actual prime orbits.

synthesis: Short multiplicative polynomials can be controlled by approximate frequency orthogonality and an exact combinatorial diagonal, enabling moment reductions such as mollification; increasing length or interaction order exposes shifted coefficient correlations, and the zeta fourth moment requires an automorphic spectral treatment of off-diagonal structure.
source_support: Conrey reduces a zero count to a mollified mean square. Soundararajan's lemma expands a short prime polynomial, splits diagonal and off-diagonal terms, and uses the length bound to absorb the latter. Conrey-Gonek identify additive-divisor correlations as the gate for long mean squares, while Motohashi replaces the elementary diagonal split with determinant classes, Kloosterman sums, and automorphic spectral decomposition for the fourth moment.
nonparaphrase_operation: Track the changing sufficient statistic: a coefficient norm and factorial diagonal at short length, shifted correlations for long polynomials, and automorphic spectral data for the fourth-moment off-diagonal.
limits: The parents use different moments, weights, and admissible lengths; additive-divisor asymptotics remain unproved in the stated regimes, and the fourth-moment machinery is not a universal solution for arbitrary high moments.
quality_reason: The synthesis states a concrete escalation of proof obligations and does not infer that one diagonal estimate, correlation conjecture, or automorphic decomposition transfers unchanged across regimes.

synthesis: A layered interface carries analytic zero control to a discrete prime witness: positivity and growth bounds exclude zeros near one, contour displacement converts zero-free width into a quantitative prime-counting estimate, finite verification can be spliced with a tail region for effective constants, and a positive theta increment certifies that some prime occurs.
source_support: Harper proves both the positivity/local-growth zero-free mechanism and the contour-shift PNT estimate. The explicit-estimate paper joins a fixed verified height to Kadiri's tail region and then converts a theta-error bound into a positive interval increment. The computation paper separately states that a finite verified height may be consumed by downstream theorems without proving global RH.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compose four typed outputs—zero exclusion, contour error, matched effective region, and monotone weighted increment—while checking that each output is only an input parameter to the next layer.
limits: Constants and ranges must be compatible and several inherited theorems lie outside these units; the finite height is not global RH, and positivity witnesses existence without identifying or counting the primes in the interval.
quality_reason: The relation is an explicit implication chain with preserved handoff conditions, not a generic claim that zero-free regions somehow imply primes or that a finite computation proves the asymptotic theory.

synthesis: A bounded zero cutoff is a resolution parameter rather than exact prime-power recovery: in the truncated explicit formula it leaves a stated contour remainder, while in the separately Gaussian-smoothed density reconstruction it produces finite-width lines and an exponentially calibrated usable x-window.
source_support: Harper gives the bounded-height zero sum for Psi with its O(x log^2 x/T) remainder. The numerical-semicalssical units distinguish full delta support from finite-width truncated lines and relate a Gaussian-damped zero cutoff to an operational x boundary. Riemann's unit proposes comparing observed residuals with individual periodic terms and using the smoother f observable.
nonparaphrase_operation: Treat cutoff height as an information-budget variable and compare what each representation preserves—aggregate residual signal or smoothed line location—against its distinct remainder or damping law.
limits: The contour remainder and Gaussian damping are different mechanisms and are not one shared error theorem; line position, shape, height, and attribution remain separate, and no finite sum uniquely assigns every fluctuation or recovers exact spikes beyond its calibrated window.
quality_reason: The cross-source relation survives because it compares two explicit cutoff interfaces while expressly rejecting their false equivalence and retaining the historical proposal as a diagnostic rather than validation.

synthesis: Prime-local arithmetic absent from a zero-statistics-only random-matrix model is retained by combining a partial Euler factor with a partial zero-side Hadamard factor; the cutoff X reallocates visible structure between the two factors, while their product is reported to remain approximately stable in a bounded numerical illustration.

The hybrid-model introduction diagnoses the missing arithmetic moment factor and proposes the partial Euler-Hadamard product, while its appendix reports two-X pointwise compensation near a high zero.
nonparaphrase_operation: Use X as a representation perturbation: observe which features move between prime and zero factors and which survive in their product, while separating the universal zero-statistical factor from prime-local arithmetic.
limits: The moment reconstruction is assumption-dependent, the pointwise compensation is an author-reported illustration without curves or residuals in the artifact, and neither leading-factor separation nor random-matrix matching establishes lower-order independence or RH.
quality_reason: The parents jointly support a specific factor-allocation mechanism, and the synthesis confines numerical stability and arithmetic/universal separation to the epistemic strength actually available.

synthesis: The proposal correctly notes that moment or marginal information alone does not determine extremes, but it unsupportedly treats a tree representation for a separate mesoscopic zeta-zero covariance matrix as the dependence structure of the log|zeta|/CUE extreme-value field and as motivation for its freezing law.
source_support: The moment units relate fixed or conjecturally growing moments to value bands and maximal-order lower bounds. The CUE units separately posit strong log|zeta| correlations, logarithmic Fourier covariance, and a conjectural freezing extreme law. The tree unit constructs a Gaussian vector for an interval-minimum covariance arising in mesoscopic fluctuations of zeta zeros; it does not identify that process with the log|zeta| landscape.
nonparaphrase_operation: A valid comparison would keep tail sensitivity, log-correlated CUE modeling, and mesoscopic zero-count covariance as distinct objects; the proposed bridge instead changes observables and covariance kernels without a source-supported map.
limits: Fixed-mode Gaussian convergence and covariance matching do not determine extreme laws, large-k moment uniformity is conjectural, and the tree is only a covariance realization for its own Gaussian process, not evidence that zeta's modulus has that genealogy.
quality_reason: Rejected for incompatible-process unification: no cited parent connects the interval-minimum tree covariance to the logarithmic modulus field or derives the freezing prediction from it, so the claimed missing dependence structure is not supported by all parents.

synthesis: Prime-power aggregation can hide an exponent-two layer that becomes leading when the aggregate is decomposed: prime squares force a deterministic center shift in quadratic-family log L-values and dominate a conditional prime-only comparison in a distinct prime-distribution argument.

limits: The two bias phenomena concern different observables, hypotheses, and averaging mechanisms; their signs and coefficients do not transfer, and Riemann's inversion is a structural antecedent rather than a proof of a universal prime-square law.
quality_reason: The synthesis identifies a concrete decomposition operation shared across the sources and explicitly preserves the incompatible settings instead of inferring one universal square-bias theorem.

synthesis: Two equivalent-criterion programs replace direct zero location by different objects: Mellin analysis converts global growth of a smoothed Mobius-weighted function into holomorphic reach, while Jensen transformation converts completed-zeta Taylor packets into an infinite hierarchy of finite real-rootedness tests. Neither representation makes the uniform RH burden finite.

The Jensen units state the all-degree/all-shift hyperbolicity equivalence, explain finite-difference extraction of limiting polynomial families, and prove only eventual hyperbolicity for each fixed degree through a short-shift saddle expansion.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compare two compressions by their quantifiers: decay over an unbounded arithmetic scale versus hyperbolicity over an unbounded two-parameter polynomial hierarchy, with each finite or local calculation leaving a global uniformity obligation.
limits: Exact exponents and coefficient normalizations are scan-sensitive; eventual fixed-degree Hermite convergence is not simultaneous hyperbolicity, and neither finitely many polynomial checks nor bounded-range decay proves RH.
quality_reason: Both sides are genuine source-stated equivalence programs, and the synthesis preserves their different transforms, two-way proof burdens, and crucial unbounded quantifiers.

synthesis: Scalar completion exposes Riemann's reflection, whereas several-variable completion must coordinate congruence channels, archimedean factors, and local correction polynomials across two summation perspectives; the resulting affine reflection geometry can then test which apparent polar loci are removable and which remain symmetry-compatible candidates.

The multiple-Dirichlet-series units construct channelwise gamma completions with finite-group invariance, characterize P and Q corrections through functional identities and summation interchange in the finite-group cases, and use reflection paths plus two-variable analyticity to remove bad-prime candidates while retaining w=3/4 only as a possible pole.
nonparaphrase_operation: Generalize completion from multiplying one scalar function by factors to solving a compatibility problem among channel representations, then use the generated reflection paths as both estimate transports and singularity-consistency tests.
limits: The several-variable construction concerns family moments and its own continuation, not classical RH; not every local correction or global continuation is supplied here, the degree-four loss of uniqueness is only a boundary signal, and reflection stability does not prove that a candidate pole exists.
quality_reason: The relation is supported at the level of explicit completion and reflection operations, preserves the different scalar and multichannel settings, and does not turn symmetry-compatible polar geometry into an established singularity or an RH result.
